heading: Learning Journey — 2026 and Beyond
description: A prerequisite-led plan: start with the foundations, select a relevant mechanism, then produce evidence that another person can inspect and reproduce.
note: Mission IDs identify stable catalog entries. They are not months, a fixed schedule or a measure of career readiness. Each area below is planned learning, not a completed qualification.

foundations.title: Threat model & requirements
foundations.description: Pin the system, map assets and trust boundaries, and define the product’s security requirements.
foundations.gate: Git, HTTP and basic Python source reasoning.

foundations.title: API ownership & permissions
foundations.description: Trace caller-to-object access and write permitted and denied request predictions.
foundations.gate: M01 plus HTTP, identity and database-filter fundamentals.

foundations.title: Secure uploads & file handling
foundations.description: Plan bounded parsing, private file access, processing failure and cleanup cases.
foundations.gate: M01/M02 plus file and HTTP fundamentals.

foundations.title: Configuration & secrets
foundations.description: Inspect effective deployment settings, listeners, privileges and the secret lifecycle.
foundations.gate: M01 plus configuration, process and network fundamentals.

foundations.title: Data flows & privacy
foundations.description: Trace synthetic fields to model, tool and log sinks; plan minimization controls.
foundations.gate: M01–M04 plus JSON and data-flow reasoning.

tracks.name: Application & product security
tracks.label: Primary direction
tracks.description: Authorization, data and action boundaries, secure delivery and reliable operations. Build relevant foundations before the selected application mechanism.
tracks.gate: Native Enterprise, retrieval and sandbox cases keep their separate availability and runtime gates.

tracks.name: Agent application security
tracks.label: Product-dependent
tracks.scope: Relevant M01–M30 foundations → M34; M38/M39 when required
tracks.description: Task-bound delegation, authenticated peers, secure tool execution, stop controls and effect reconciliation.
tracks.gate: M34 needs M11/M13/M15/M25/M27. Computer-use and malicious-use specialties are added only when the product responsibility requires them.

tracks.name: Model & training security
tracks.label: Optional specialty
tracks.description: Valid robustness, training/artifact trust and model-privacy experiments on known synthetic data with held-out evaluation.
tracks.gate: Requires ML/statistics, a real pinned small model, approved compute, split provenance and known membership where needed.

tracks.name: Inference platform security
tracks.label: Optional specialty
tracks.description: Selected serving-engine management, worker, artifact and cache boundaries.
tracks.gate: Requires an actual selected engine/build, suitable resources and its observed runtime architecture. Source and fixture work cannot prove native isolation.

tracks.name: Security program ownership
tracks.label: Optional senior scope
tracks.description: Accountable decisions, maintenance and recurrence prevention across products after reviewable technical work.
tracks.gate: Simulated program records remain labeled. Real program ownership needs actual responsibilities, stakeholders and sustained operating evidence.

depths.name: Deep
depths.description: Trace a selected mechanism, predict outcomes, reproduce when feasible, review the control and transfer the principle. Stop at the declared reviewable boundary.

depths.name: Working
depths.description: Use a selected component safely and validate a known outcome plus a legitimate or negative control.

depths.name: Reference
depths.description: Explain when a component fits, what evidence it offers and its prerequisites. Installation is not required.

queueNote: Plan one active primary assignment. When a runtime prerequisite is blocked, continue useful source/design work and keep runtime conclusions unverified.

focusAreas.title: AI application authorization and privacy
focusAreas.description: Caller-to-object authority, revocation and minimizing data at model, tool and log boundaries.

focusAreas.title: RAG ingestion, retrieval and data lifecycle
focusAreas.description: Provenance, access filters, context ownership, deletion and policy-aware restoration.

focusAreas.title: MCP, agent permissions and secure tool execution
focusAreas.description: Identity-bound tools, exact action approval, least privilege and independently enforced stop.

focusAreas.title: Prompt-injection and security regression evaluation
focusAreas.description: Hostile input measured at the consequential boundary, with validated scoring and legitimate controls.

focusAreas.title: Secure delivery, telemetry and incident recovery
focusAreas.description: Versioned controls, privacy-aware events, reconciliation, safe rollback and reproducible handover.

skills.name: Python
skills.description: Source reasoning, bounded helpers and synthetic fixtures.

skills.name: HTTP / API security
skills.description: Request authority, ownership, filters and outbound policy.

skills.name: Git
skills.description: Source pins, reviewed changes and reproducible history.

skills.name: Authentication / OAuth
skills.description: Sessions, audience, consent and revoked grants.

skills.name: Docker & configuration
skills.description: Effective settings, runtime contracts and image identity.

skills.name: RAG
skills.description: Ingestion, authorized retrieval and derived-copy lifecycle.

skills.name: Threat modeling
skills.description: Product needs, trust boundaries and adverse outcomes.

skills.name: Evaluation
skills.description: Ground truth, valid trials and security/utility tradeoffs.

skills.name: Security reporting
skills.description: Finding classification, limitations, retesting and handover.
